end_anchor: dplyr::select(sample_id, major_area, year, month, catch, species_code)
grain_in: STATION_BS: one row per bag-seine haul (sample_id); bagseine: one row per haul x species catch record
grain_out: station: one row per haul in major areas 1 to 8; data: one row per haul x species catch record, all areas
units_out: station: identifiers and dates only; data: counts of individuals
operation: The region's true first statement is the load of data.Rdata on the line above start_anchor, which carries a trailing comment and so cannot be an anchor; the region then subsets STATION_BS to four columns and restricts hauls to major_area 1 to 8, and subsets bagseine to six columns. The column selections are absorbed as reformatting; the major_area filter is the decision, and it is applied to the haul table only, not to the catch table. The rm() housekeeping line below end_anchor is deliberately outside every region: it drops unused objects and changes nothing computed.
settings: major_area kept: 1:8; station columns: sample_id, major_area, year, month; catch columns: sample_id, major_area, year, month, catch, species_code; major_area on the catch table is carried but never used
na_behavior: A haul with NA major_area fails %in% and is dropped silently from station, indistinguishable from a haul in areas 9 or above. Hauls dropped here still exist in data, so their catch records continue to influence the rarity count in the next node.

grain_in: one row per haul x species catch record
grain_out: one species_code per element of a character/numeric vector
units_out: species identifiers, selected on a count of positive records
operation: Counts, for each species, the number of catch records with catch > 0 by passing the logical as the count weight, then keeps species with 5 or fewer such records as the set to drop. The count runs over the full catch table, so records from major areas outside 1 to 8 and from years outside 1992 to 2024 contribute to the rarity decision even though those rows are excluded from every later step.
settings: threshold n <= 5; weight = (catch > 0), so n is a count of positive records rather than of hauls or of individuals; no grouping by area, year, or period, so rarity is judged across the whole data set
na_behavior: If catch is NA the weight is NA and the species total n becomes NA; filter(n <= 5) evaluates NA as not TRUE, so that species is not flagged as rare and is retained. A record with catch = 0 and a record with catch = NA both contribute nothing to n and are not distinguishable afterwards.

grain_in: one row per haul x species catch record
grain_out: one row per haul x species catch record, rare species removed
operation: Drops every catch record belonging to a flagged rare species, changing which species population the rest of the script describes.
settings: negated %in% match on species_code; no other criterion
na_behavior: A record with NA species_code does not match rare_sp and is kept; it later becomes its own column in the wide matrix and its own species level downstream.

section: 2. Sample x species matrix with zeros
grain_in: one row per haul x species catch record
grain_out: one row per haul x species
units_out: counts of individuals per haul per species
operation: Aggregates catch records to one abundance per haul per species by summing catch. This collapses any within-haul subdivision of the same species (for example separate length or size records) into a single total; whether such subdivision exists in the source cannot be told from the code alone.
settings: sum(catch) with no na.rm argument, so the default na.rm = FALSE applies; .groups = drop
na_behavior: Because na.rm is not set, a single NA catch makes the whole haul x species abundance NA. That NA is not filled by values_fill in the next node (which only fills absent combinations) and is instead converted to 0 by the replace_na in the next node, so a missing measurement is silently turned into an observed zero.

section: 2. Sample x species matrix with zeros
grain_in: one row per haul x species
grain_out: one row per haul listed in station (major areas 1 to 8), one column per retained species
units_out: counts of individuals, with structural zeros
operation: Reshapes the haul x species table to a wide matrix and then left joins it onto the distinct haul list from station, so that the haul list, not the catch table, determines which rows exist. Hauls in station with no catch record at all receive all-zero rows via replace_na. The pivot_wider is absorbed as a reshape; the join is the decision, because it defines true absences and also drops any haul that appears in the catch data but not in station or lies outside areas 1 to 8.
settings: values_fill = 0 and names_prefix = sp_ in the pivot; join key sample_id; distinct() on sample_id, major_area, year, month; replace_na(0) across all sp_ columns
na_behavior: Three different causes collapse into the same 0 and are not distinguishable downstream: a species not caught in a haul that was fished, a haul with no catch record at all, and an abundance that was NA because catch was NA. If station holds duplicate sample_id rows with differing major_area, year, or month, distinct() keeps both and the haul is counted twice.

section: Period scheme: 11 periods, 3-year bins over 1992 to 2024
grain_out: one row per calendar year from 1992 to 2024
units_out: a year and its period label
operation: Defines the period scheme: 11 consecutive 3-year bins covering 1992 to 2024, with a stopifnot check that the bin lengths sum to the year span, and builds the year-to-period lookup joined in later nodes. period_is_partial is set FALSE for every year and is never read again in this script.
settings: start_year 1992; end_year 2024; period_lengths rep(3, 11); factor levels P1 to P11 in that order; bins are calendar-year aligned and non-overlapping
na_behavior: Years outside 1992 to 2024 are simply absent from the lookup, so a later left join gives them NA period and they are removed by the filter(!is.na(period)) steps. A year absent from the data and a year outside the scheme are not distinguishable after the join.

section: 3. Long data with species_code numeric, seasons, and period
grain_in: one row per haul, species in columns
grain_out: one row per haul x species, with period and season attached
operation: Restricts hauls to 1992 to 2024, joins the period label, reshapes the wide matrix back to long form recovering species_code from the column name, and assigns a season from the calendar month. The pivot_longer and the unused mid-month date column are absorbed as reformatting; the year filter, the join, and the season assignment are the decisions. Winter is built from months 12, 1, and 2 of the same calendar year, so a December is grouped with the January and February that precede it rather than the ones that follow, while the header comment describes the season as DJF; the code and the comment disagree on what a winter is. The closing filter(!is.na(period)) cannot remove anything, because the year filter above it already guarantees a period match.
settings: year bounds start_year and end_year; season map 12,1,2 Winter / 3-5 Spring / 6-8 Summer / 9-11 Fall with no default branch; season factor levels Winter, Spring, Summer, Fall; species_code coerced to integer twice, once in names_transform and once in mutate
na_behavior: A month outside 1 to 11 and not equal to 12 falls through every case_when branch and gets NA season; such rows are not dropped here and survive to the stratum filter, where they can only fail. NA period is impossible at this point.

section: 4. Identify and keep only fully sampled strata (n_samples == 180)
grain_in: one row per haul in station (major areas 1 to 8)
grain_out: one row per haul with period and season attached
operation: Applies the same year restriction, period join, and season assignment to the haul table so that hauls can be counted independently of the catch data. This is the same code as the season and period assignment in the long-data node but a separate node, because the input is the haul table rather than the species matrix.
settings: same year bounds and same season map as the long-data node; the full lookup is joined, so period_num and period_is_partial are carried along
na_behavior: A month outside the mapped values gives NA season, which forms its own group in the count below and can never reach 180. NA period is impossible after the year filter, so the trailing filter removes nothing.

section: 4. Identify and keep only fully sampled strata (n_samples == 180)
grain_in: one row per haul with period and season
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season that is retained
units_out: a count of distinct hauls, used as a keep/drop flag
operation: Counts distinct hauls in each bay x period x season and keeps only strata with exactly 180, which is the count a fully sampled 3-year period gives at 20 hauls per month x 3 months x 3 years; the arithmetic behind 180 is not stated in the code. The message block is absorbed because it only prints a tally and computes nothing carried forward.
settings: n_distinct(sample_id) as the haul count; equality test n_samples == 180, so a stratum with more than 180 hauls is dropped as well as one with fewer; the printed message describes the dropped strata as having fewer than 180, which the code does not guarantee
na_behavior: Strata whose season is NA form their own groups and fail the equality test. A stratum absent from station entirely produces no row and is dropped, which is not distinguishable from a stratum that was sampled but incompletely.

section: 4. Identify and keep only fully sampled strata (n_samples == 180)
grain_in: one row per haul x species with period and season
grain_out: one row per haul x species, restricted to fully sampled strata
operation: Restricts the analysis data to the strata that passed the 180-haul test, changing which population the rest of the script describes, and overwrites monthly_sp in place so the unfiltered version is no longer available.
na_behavior: Rows with NA season or NA period match nothing and are dropped silently, alongside rows dropped for incomplete sampling; the two reasons are not distinguishable afterwards.
notes: Up to this point. The code is the same as that in "c"

section: Optional but recommended: keep only fully sampled strata
grain_in: one row per haul in station (major areas 1 to 8)
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season that is retained
units_out: a count of distinct hauls, used as a keep/drop flag
operation: Recomputes station_strat and valid_strata from scratch and overwrites both objects. The valid_strata block here is character for character identical to the earlier one; the station_strat block differs only in that the lookup is reduced to year and period before the join, so period_num and period_is_partial are not carried. The set of retained strata is therefore the same, and this node exists in the table because the code runs twice, not because the result changes. The intermediate valid_strata assignment is not absorbed into the surrounding region as reformatting: it is an aggregation with a threshold, and it is included here because it is a byte-identical repeat of an earlier node rather than a new decision.
settings: same as the first pass: year bounds, same season map, n_distinct(sample_id), equality test at 180; the only difference is select(year, period) applied to the lookup before the join
na_behavior: Identical to the first pass. Because both objects are overwritten, anything a reader verified about the earlier versions no longer describes the objects in memory after this point.

section: Optional but recommended: keep only fully sampled strata
grain_in: one row per haul x species, already restricted to fully sampled strata
grain_out: one row per haul x species, restricted to fully sampled strata
operation: Applies the stratum filter a second time, to a monthly_sp that was already filtered by the same criterion at the earlier semi_join. Given the recomputed valid_strata selects the same strata, this removes nothing and only makes a renamed copy; it would matter only if the second valid_strata differed from the first.
na_behavior: No rows with NA keys remain by this point, so nothing is dropped for that reason here.

grain_in: one row per haul x species
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season x month x year x species
operation: Aggregates hauls to a monthly community: total abundance summed over hauls, hauls counted, and the two combined into a mean per haul. This is the arithmetic that converts a count into a rate and so makes cells with different haul counts comparable. n_hauls is counted within each species group, which is safe only because the haul x species matrix is complete after the zero fill; if it were not, species-specific denominators would differ within the same cell.
settings: sum with na.rm = TRUE; n_distinct(sample_id) as the denominator; if_else guard returning 0 when n_hauls is not greater than 0, which cannot occur because a group only exists when it has at least one row; .groups = drop
na_behavior: na.rm = TRUE means a cell in which every abundance were NA would sum to 0 and produce a mean of 0 rather than a missing value, indistinguishable from a genuine absence. In practice no NAs reach here, because the zero fill upstream already converted them.

grain_in: one row per year x species within a single bay x period x season x month cell
grain_out: one row per consecutive year pair within that cell
operation: Defines the helper that turns one month-cell into consecutive-year dissimilarities: it pivots to a year x species matrix filling absent combinations with 0, calls vegan::vegdist for Bray-Curtis over all year pairs, then keeps only pairs (t, t+1) in which both years are present. Because the pairing is done inside a cell and cells are period-bounded, the pair that straddles a period boundary is never formed. The as.matrix conversion and the rownames assignment are absorbed as reformatting that only carries the result to the lookup.
settings: method = bray in vegdist; values_fill = 0 in the pivot; arrange(year) before matrix conversion; pairs defined as year2 = year1 + 1 and required to be present in the cell; no abundance transformation or standardisation before the distance, so the index is dominated by abundant species
na_behavior: The function returns a zero-row tibble in two distinct situations, fewer than 2 distinct years in the cell and no consecutive pair among the years present, and these collapse into the same empty result downstream: the cell simply contributes no rows and is not distinguishable from a cell that was never sampled. If a year's community vector is all zeros, vegdist returns NaN for every pair involving it and that NaN is passed through as a bray value rather than flagged.

end_anchor: arrange(major_area, period, season, month, year1, year2)
grain_in: one row per bay x period x season x month x year x species
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season x month x consecutive year pair
operation: Call site of the helper: splits the mean-per-haul table by bay x period x season x month and applies the dissimilarity function to each group, so year pairs are always compared within the same calendar month and never across months. The select inside group_modify and the rename of bray to bray_consecutive are absorbed as reformatting. The species set is rebuilt inside each group, so the community matrix has different columns in different cells; this does not change Bray-Curtis, which ignores species absent from both years, but it does mean the matrices are not comparable objects across cells.
settings: grouping keys major_area, period, season, month; the empty-result branch inside group_modify returns the same empty tibble the function already returns and so changes nothing; final arrange for readability only
na_behavior: Groups producing no rows disappear without trace, whether from a single sampled year or from no consecutive pair. NaN dissimilarities from empty communities are kept as values in bray_consecutive and are treated as missing only by the na.rm arguments in the next node.

section: Aggregate to the stratum (bay x period x season)
grain_in: one row per bay x period x season x month x year pair
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season
operation: Two aggregations in one region: first the mean dissimilarity across the months of a season for each year pair, then the mean across the year pairs within the period. Both are unweighted, so a year pair supported by one month counts as much as one supported by three, and n_months_used and n_pairs are carried as diagnostics rather than used as weights. Within a 3-year period only the two internal year pairs exist, so the transition between consecutive periods is never measured anywhere in the script.
settings: na.rm = TRUE at both levels; n_months_used counts finite values, so NaN and Inf are excluded but the count of months attempted is not recorded; n_pairs is a plain row count expected to be 2; grouping keys major_area, period, season
na_behavior: A year pair whose months are all NaN gives a mean of NaN with n_months_used 0, and that pair is then dropped by the outer na.rm, so the stratum value can rest on a single pair without that being visible except through n_pairs and mean_months_per_pair. If every pair in a stratum is NaN, the outer mean over an empty set returns NaN. A stratum built from partial months and one built from all three are not distinguishable from bray_bc alone.

grain_in: one row per bay x period x season x month x year pair; one row per bay x period x season
grain_out: two CSV files on disk with the same grains
operation: Creates a results directory if absent and writes both tables, stamping the file names with the run date rather than with a data version, so two runs on the same day overwrite each other and runs on different days accumulate. The exported stratum table carries n_pairs and mean_months_per_pair as well as bray_bc, which the header comment does not list.
settings: output directory results under script_dir; date tag from Sys.Date() formatted %Y-%m-%d; file stems beta_bray_pairs_monthly_ and beta_bray_bay_period_season_; write_csv defaults, so NaN is written as NA
na_behavior: NaN values produced upstream are written as empty or NA fields and are not distinguishable in the file from a stratum that was never computed.
